record.paper_title: Some open problems on well-filtered spaces and sober spaces
record.original_question: Let Co-Sob be the category of co-sober spaces with continuous mappings. Is Co-Sob reflective in Top0?

evidence.quote: Question 9.8. Is Co-Sob reflective in Top0 ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbf{Top}_0$ denote the category whose objects are $T_0$ topological spaces and whose morphisms are continuous maps. For a topological space $X$, a nonempty subset $A \subseteq X$ is called irreducible if whenever $A \subseteq F_1 \cup F_2$ with $F_1, F_2$ closed, then $A \subseteq F_1$ or $A \subseteq F_2$. A subset $K \subseteq X$ is saturated if it equals the intersection of its open neighborhoods (equivalently, $K$ is an upper set in the specialization order). A nonempty compact saturated set $K$ is called $k$-irreducible (or supercompact) if whenever $K \subseteq U_1 \cup U_2$ with $U_1, U_2$ open, then $K \subseteq U_1$ or $K \subseteq U_2$. 

A topological space $X$ is called co-sober if every $k$-irreducible compact saturated subset of $X$ is the saturation $\uparrow\! x = \{y \in X : x \le_{sp} y\}$ of some point $x \in X$, where $\le_{sp}$ denotes the specialization order. Let $\mathbf{Co\text{-}Sob}$ be the full subcategory of $\mathbf{Top}_0$ whose objects are the co-sober $T_0$ spaces.

Determine whether $\mathbf{Co\text{-}Sob}$ is a reflective subcategory of $\mathbf{Top}_0$; that is, decide whether the inclusion functor $\mathbf{Co\text{-}Sob} \hookrightarrow \mathbf{Top}_0$ has a left adjoint.
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches surface related work showing that certain neighboring categories (e.g., quasisober spaces and weakly sober spaces) are not reflective in $\mathbf{Top}_0$, and that sober Scott spaces need not be co-sober. However, no source was found that explicitly resolves whether the category of co-sober spaces is reflective in $\mathbf{Top}_0$, so the status appears unresolved as of available information.

status_evidence.title: Non-reflective categories of some kinds of weakly sober spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Neither the category of all quasisober spaces nor that of all weakly sober spaces is reflective in Top0.
status_evidence.claim: Related neighboring categories are known to be non-reflective in Top0, but co-sober is not addressed in the abstract.

status_evidence.title: Sober Scott spaces are not always co-sober
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs a dcpo whose Scott space is sober but not co-sober.
status_evidence.claim: Co-sober spaces form a strictly smaller class than sober spaces in general.
